please document what you tested.  Knowing you tested on an EVB is useful, but doesn't tell me how I can make sure I see the same behavior.

Sure @ed@tanous.net . 

Test 1 – Valid Image Upload

Request:

Method: POST

URL: https://<bmc-ip>/redfish/v1/UpdateService/update

Authentication: Basic Auth (root / 0penBmc)

Body: binary → select valid firmware image

Expected Result:

HTTP 202 Accepted

Task created at /redfish/v1/TaskService/Tasks/<TaskId>

Task state transitions normally (Running → Completed)

Observed Result:

HTTP 202 returned

Task created successfully

Update flow completed without errors

Test 2 – Invalid / Corrupted Image Upload

Request:

Method: POST

URL: https://<bmc-ip>/redfish/v1/UpdateService/update

Authentication: Basic Auth

Body: binary → select corrupted or invalid file



Expected Result (After This Change):

Immediate HTTP 4xx error response

No task created

Observed Result:

HTTP 4xx returned immediately

No entry created under /redfish/v1/TaskService/Tasks
Overall, I suspect this is solving a problem that needs handled in the backend.

@ed@tanous.net This commit wont allow to create a task itself unless the valid image is selected during POST operation in POSTMAN of the URI : https://<bmc-ip>/redfish/v1/UpdateService/update  that is why we avoided 500 internal error that would create a task in  /redfish/v1/TaskService/Tasks

Why do we care?  500 means we have a bug in error handling somewhere.  Lets fix it at the source of where it's called, not by adding new rules upstream.

One character of a firmware update would cause the same bug.  BMCWEB doesn't have the ability to validate "is this payload correct", so we need the backend to tell us.
Okay @ed@tanous.net i will withdraw this MR changes. Thanks
You look like you've ignored this.  Please don't ignore it.
Could you please elaborate what i have ignored?

I think the previous message here was correct.  The internal service failed to provide updates and has locked up.

If we want to provide this information to the user, do it via the backend service.

Hi @ed@tanous.net We added this message to handle cases where a user uploads an invalid image during the POST operation to /redfish/v1/UpdateService/update.

With this change, the service immediately returns an error and prevents creation of a task at /redfish/v1/TaskService/Tasks/<TaskId>. Previously, a task would still be created, and only afterward would it fail with a 500 Internal Server Error. 

Verified that uploading a valid image successfully creates a task and completes the update flow as expected.

Verified that uploading an invalid or corrupted image now returns an appropriate error response without creating a task.

Confirmed that no /redfish/v1/TaskService/Tasks/<TaskId> entry is created in the failure scenario.
Done
